instructions: StationGod reads and changes a running Stationeers world. Each tool is a verb; most take what (the kind of thing) and share option names: find (lists), inspect (one thing in detail), survey (an area or network), read (live values), write (set values), plan (work out, change nothing), check (rules), build, swap (existing pieces), remove, move, trade, show (draw for the player), undo, server. help {verb, what} gives one in full. Targets: id (one, a list, or a ref "r3" from an earlier reply), near + radius, box, room, network. 'this', 'that' or 'here' is the thing the crosshair is on: inspect {what: "looking_at"}. build, swap, remove, move, trade, undo and cheats only report until confirm: true, and so does any write given a ref or network; ask the user before a cheat. For many things, give id a list or a ref. Shaping on every verb: fields, omit, list_limits, output_file, repeat (a ref: that call again), whole: true (lifts the cut of a reply over 12 KB; pages stay pages). For work across many replies or many targets, run_script. A script changes nothing unless the run has confirm: true. If the user says stop or hold: server {what: 'stop'}.

tools.name: find
tools.description: List things in the world or an area, filtered, a page at a time, nearest first. Read only.

what.description: thing: any object: structures, devices, tanks, loose items, players, animals; item: stackable items and kits with quantity and holders, anywhere: ground, carried, stored, machine stock, silos; a kit such as Kit (Battery Large) is an item to find and move, a built structure is not; group_by sums them; device: devices with logic, in the world or on one gateway's data networks; container: outermost holders with at least one item: lockers, crates, machines, a backpack on the floor; frame: outer frames (a face on outside air), with exposed faces and airtightness; pad: landing pads for traders and rockets (not power or teleport pads), by the game's checks: size, runway, which ships fit; water: canisters, tanks, devices and pipe networks holding water or steam, largest first; ore: deep miner spots: the ore profile at a point, and the nearest spots holding given ores; food: every food and drink: nutrition, hydration, decay, totals; plant: plants in trays, planters and stations: stage, health, problems, time to harvest; room: closed rooms measured cell by cell: volume, pressure, temperature, gases; or the room one thing is in; gateway: the device scopes: 'world' and each StationGod Gateway with its status; damaged: damaged and broken things in the world, worst first

prefab.description: Prefab: a whole name, a hash, or parts with * ('*Battery*', '*Tank*Insulated*': each part, any order); or a list of them.

category.description: Only this kind of thing. Default any.

location.description: thing: ground, player, stored, built or world (players, animals). Default any. item: Where the item is. Default any.

near.description: thing, item: Centre: [x, y, z], "player", "looking_at" or a thing's id (its position); with radius. container, frame, damaged: "player" only. ore: The point to report and search from; default the player's position.

box.description: Two corners [[x, y, z], [x, y, z]].

within.description: Only items inside this holder at any depth (and its machine stock or silo store).

group_by.description: holder: sum per holder and prefab; prefab: sum per prefab; place: per prefab split into ground, carried, stored, machine stock and silo, with top holders.

id.description: plant: One plant, in full. room: A thing: only the room it is in. Any what that takes an id takes a list: one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, ...} or {index, ok, reference_id, error}], count, success_count, error_count}; a bad id is a row with error.

tools.name: inspect
tools.description: Describe one thing, or a few by id, in detail. Read only.

what.description: device: a device: logic types it reads and writes, writable ones by name, rocket, umbilical and uplink details; prefab: a buildable prefab before it stands anywhere: placement kind, turns, cells, ports; slots: a device's slots: occupants, what each takes, slot logic values; contents: any holder's slots and what is in them, nested (a locker, machine, suit; 'player' for the player); health: damage state of things, or of every piece of a network, worst first; connections: one pipe, cable, chute or device: its ends and what each joins; atmosphere: the gas or liquid one thing holds: canister, tank, a rocket's tanks (rocket id or name), suit, pipe or pad network, a device's networks; reagents: the reagents a furnace, centrifuge, mixer or microwave holds; genes: the genes of plants, seeds and produce; chip: a circuit holder's chip: status (line, registers, stack, pins, errors, Lua log), source, selectors. Any device's memory: read memory; screen: what a ScriptedScreens screen shows: surfaces and one surface's elements; rocket: every rocket now, or one by id or name ('Tanker'): position, target, mass, fuel, engines, landing confidence, cargo, power. For a flight or landing check use plan flight; vault: what each Ingot Vault stores, and every Remote Vault's link; looking_at: what the player's crosshair is on, and where a longer look ray lands; player: the player's hunger and thirst: nutrition, hydration, drain, time left; planet: the planet's atmosphere: gases, pressure, temperature, day range, sea, ice caps; weather: the storm schedule, weather events and season; job: one build, removal, swap or gas move by its id (place-41), or a script run (script-14): running, queued or finished. With no id: runs with notices pending (stopped or killed with something left, writes not done, or done and not yet seen); controllers: controllers: what can write or override a device: IC chips (through their pins, and batch writers reaching it over its data network), logic writer and memory structures, Lua screen scripts, and writers the hub knows (the dashboard's hub, other runs). A write or report on a driven device carries driven_by naming the controller

id.description: device, slots, connections, reagents: An id, a list, a ref ('r3'), or "looking_at". contents: A holder's id or "player". health: Up to 256 things. atmosphere: A thing, a pipe or landing pad network, or an atmosphere id. genes: Up to 256 plants, seeds or produce. chip: The circuit holder, worn holder, Lua board or the chip. screen: One id, or "looking_at" (the thing the crosshair is on). rocket: A rocket's id, name, network or any part; left out, every rocket. vault: One Ingot or Remote Vault; default every vault. controllers: The device(s). job: A job id (place-12, run-4, remove-3...), a script run (script-14), a gas transfer id, or "paste"; left out, runs with notices pending. Any what that takes an id takes a list: one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, ...} or {index, ok, reference_id, error}], count, success_count, error_count}; a bad id is a row with error.

prefab.description: prefab: Whole prefab name or hash. contents: Only slots holding this prefab (part with *) at any depth.

network.description: A network: its id, a piece or device on it, or {id, port}.

targets.description: selectors: devices to evaluate; default those on the holder's data network.

max_wait.description: How long this reply waits (default 30), at most your client's timeout; the job or run goes on.

Any what that takes an id takes a list: one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, ...} or {index, ok, reference_id, error}], count, success_count, error_count}; a bad id is a row with error.

prefab.description: Prefab: a whole name, a hash, or parts with * ('*Battery*', '*Tank*Insulated*': each part, any order); or a list of them.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Set values and states: logic, chip source, pins and run state, screen presses, labels, paint, uplinks. Ids you type out act at once; a ref or network reports until confirm: true. A write on a device a chip or another writer drives warns driven_by. memory, battery and genes are cheats: they report until confirm: true.

what.description: logic: logic values on devices, as a chip or console writes them; answers previous and read-back values; memory: up to 512 values into a device's memory from start, as a chip's put does; chip: a circuit holder's chip: write source (IC10 or Lua), set pins d0-d5, or pause, step, resume, restart; screen: touch a control on a ScriptedScreens screen, as a player's touch does; label: rename things as the hand Labeller does; empty name gives back the game's name; paint: paint things as a spray can does; network: a pipe's id, or a device's with kind, paints that network's pieces; with no target, list the colours; flight_log: start, stop or clear a rocket flight recorder (server state; never the world); read it with read flight_log; uplink: point a Logic Rocket Uplink at a Logic Rocket Downlink; battery: set the charge of batteries and cells: full by default, or a ratio or joules; genes: edit plant genes as the Gene Splicer does

id.description: logic: Device(s) or a ref; every one gets logic = value. memory, genes: An id, a list, or "looking_at". chip, screen: One id, or "looking_at" (the thing the crosshair is on). label: One id; a list or a ref names each '<label> 1', '<label> 2' in id order. paint: Things to paint the one color, or a ref. flight_log: A rocket's id, name, network or any part; left out when there is one rocket. uplink: The uplink. battery: Batteries or cells (up to 256). Any what that takes an id takes a list: one row per id, {results: [{index, ok, reference_id, ...} or {index, ok, reference_id, error}], count, success_count, error_count}; a bad id is a row with error. chip, screen, uplink and flight_log take one id: a list is refused, naming run_script.

writes.description: Separate writes, each {id, logic, value}, applied in order.

allow.description: ["lint"]: a write that turns on or opens a vent, valve or pump runs the network lint rules (no oxidiser vented outdoors, fuel mix temperature) on the network it opens to, and is refused on a problem unless lint is allowed.

confirm.description: true acts; left out, it reports.

code.description: The complete program: IC10, or Lua for a Lua chip.

pins.description: {d0..d5: device id or null}; pins left out keep their device.

labels.description: Several renames, each {id, label}, in order.

A script run gets sg.Stopped (a BaseException) once, at its next sg call (at once inside sg.wait or sg.watch), so its finally blocks run: after it, reads and writes act, while waits and watches raise at once. The worker is killed 5 s after the stop (longer while an sg call is in flight, never past 30 s), or on a second stop. A running job is allowed to settle

tools.name: run_script
tools.description:
Run Python 3.10 against the game: one call made of verb calls. sg.<verb>('what', **options) is the direct call: same options, same reply keys (a dict).
A script changes nothing unless the run has confirm: true. Seen targets: ids this session's replies showed you (direct replies, report rows, a finished run's printed or returned value), any int or str constant in the code, selectors written in the code (a network, a spread, sg.ref('r7')), and what the run builds. Three routes:
- run_script {code}: a report run. Every write reports (report_only: True) and nothing changes. The report lists every target [id or cell, name, current -> new]; builds report placed: []. It begins: script-14 REPORT: nothing changed; run_script {repeat: "script-14", confirm: true} does it.
- run_script {code, confirm: true}: acts as it goes on seen targets. An unseen target before anything acted: the run goes on as a report and its reply is that report. After an act: the run stops with sg.Stopped (a BaseException); only held restores and the finally it unwinds through still act; the stop reply lists the remaining targets as report rows (now seen) and says repeat, or undo script-N first.
- run_script {repeat: "script-14", confirm: true}: runs the code again on fresh reads; the report's rows are seen. Logic values may differ (DIFFERS FROM REPORT in the footer); [cannot undo] writes must match the report's arguments.
confirm inside the code is refused.
Give id a list, not a loop of calls:
  r = sg.find('thing', prefab='*Light*', box=[...], fields=['reference_id', 'display_name'])
  ids = [t['reference_id'] for t in r['things']]
  sg.write('logic', id=ids, logic='On', value=0)
Build, then act on what was built (report it, then repeat it):
  b = sg.build('structure', placements=[...])
  for h in b['placed']: sg.write('logic', id=h, logic='On', value=1)   # placed: [] in a report run
Hold a value while waiting; restored on exit, on stop, and at session end:
  with sg.hold(pump, 'On', 1, after=0):
      rows, met = sg.watch([{'id': tank, 'logic': 'Pressure'}], until=lambda r: r[0]['value'] >= 8000, timeout=480)
  return met                                            # or a final bare expression
sg.wait(s); sg.ref('r7'); sg.help('read', 'logic'); sg.help('scripts') has the full API. Errors raise sg.Error(code, message, fix, maybe_ran).
Reply wait: 30 s for confirmed runs, up to 600 s for report and read-only runs; a longer run answers script-N running (follow with inspect {what: 'job', id}); stop: server {what: 'stop', id}.
Footer: writes by outcome, DIFFERS FROM REPORT, WARNINGS (driven_by), CLEANUP, undo script-N, cost.

code.description: Python 3.10 source, run as a function body.

confirm.description: true: writes act, on targets you have seen. Left out: a report run; nothing acts.

repeat.description: A report run's id ('script-14'): run its code again on fresh reads; with confirm: true its reported targets are seen and act.

max_wait.description: How long this reply waits (default 30), at most your client's timeout; the run goes on.
